title: Massachusetts temporary placement of a substance in Schedule I by order
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 2A(a), NOTWITHSTANDING SECTION 2, THE COMMISSIONER MAY, BY ORDER, PLACE A SUBSTANCE IN SCHEDULE I ON A TEMPORARY BASIS if the commissioner finds: (i) it is necessary to avoid an imminent hazard to the public safety; (ii) it is necessary for the preservation of the public health, safety or general welfare; (iii) the substance is not listed in any other schedule identified in section 3; (iv) no exception is in effect for the substance pursuant to section 4; and (v) the substance is not excluded under s. 2(c). Under s. 2A(b), before finding an imminent hazard to the public safety the commissioner shall consider the substance's actual or relative potential for abuse and its history and current patterns of abuse. Under s. 2A(c) an order issued under s. 2A(a) SHALL BE AN EMERGENCY REGULATION subject to section 3 of chapter 30A, no further approval by designated persons or bodies is required before it becomes effective, and THE EMERGENCY REGULATION MAY REMAIN IN EFFECT FOR UP TO 1 YEAR. Under s. 2A(d) the order takes effect upon the completion of a 14-DAY NOTICE PERIOD, which begins when the order is published on the department of public health's website or by any other means the commissioner may deem necessary. Under s. 2A(f) the commissioner shall forward a copy of the order to the attorney general of the United States to request temporary placement of the substance in schedule I under 21 U.S.C. 811(h).
exam_relevance: Tests that Massachusetts can control a substance on its own initiative, so a statement that the Massachusetts schedules simply are the federal lists holds only as far as the current text of 105 CMR 700.002 and the orders in force.

numeric_facts.fact: Maximum period a temporary Schedule I emergency regulation may remain in effect
Notice period before an order under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 2A(a) takes effect
numeric_facts.conditions: Beginning when the order is published on the department of public health's website or by any other means the commissioner deems necessary

exceptions: The commissioner's findings under s. 2A(a) include that the substance is not listed in any other schedule identified in section 3, that no exception under section 4 is in effect for it, and that it is not excluded under s. 2(c).
common_confusions: Treating the Massachusetts schedules as incapable of differing from the federal lists, when s. 2A allows a temporary Schedule I placement by order and s. 2(a1/2) allows deletion or rescheduling by regulation.
Reading the temporary placement as permanent, when the emergency regulation may remain in effect for up to 1 year.
Assuming the order is effective on issuance, when it takes effect upon completion of a 14-day notice period.
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 2A(a) through (d) and (f) read in the current text on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
